chunks: A number of our companions narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from some of his companions from Abu Ummarah who said:

Hammad ibn Abi Hanifah, when he met me, would say, 'Repeat your hadith to me so I may narrate it.' I said, 'It has been narrated to us that a worshipper from the Children of Israel, when he reached the utmost limit in worship, would become one who walked about attending to the needs of people, attending to what would benefit them.'

key_terms.حَمَّادُ بْنُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ: Hammad ibn Abi Hanifah, a prominent early jurist
key_terms.مَشَّاءً فِي حَوَائِجِ النَّاسِ: One who walks about attending to the needs of people

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between intense worship and serving people's needs in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the transition from solitary devotion to active social service, illustrating that true spiritual maturity manifests in attending to the needs of the community. Hammad ibn Abi Hanifah’s request to repeat the tradition underscores the importance of preserving this specific link between worship (ibadah) and social responsibility (khidmah) within the chain of transmission.
